translation: It is precisely below qian, above kun, west of zhen, east of dui, the place of intercourse of kan and li, at the exact center of the heaven and earth of the human body, where the eight vessels, nine orifices, twelve channels, and fifteen collaterals converge; in the empty space there is one orifice, hanging empty like a millet pearl, which the medical books call the Ren and Du two vessels. This is where the primordial qi is engendered and where the true breath arises; if the practitioner of elixir cultivation does not understand this orifice, then the true breath is not engendered and spiritual transformation has no foundation. Yu Yan's commentary on the Cantong Qi says: The blood and qi of the human body circulate back and forth, day and night without stopping; the medical books have the Ren and Du two vessels, and if a person can open these two vessels, then all the hundred vessels are open.
